previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a patient with cholangiocarcinoma and recent history of E. coli bacteremia and C. difficile infection, was admitted with high fevers and chills following fiducial marker placement for Cyberknife radiation. He was found to have recurrent E. coli bacteremia with a multidrug-resistant pattern, leading to a diagnosis of sepsis. He was treated with intravenous meropenem and oral vancomycin, the latter continued to prevent C. difficile recurrence. His fevers resolved after two days, and he stabilized with correction of electrolyte imbalances. A PICC line was placed for outpatient administration of ertapenem. His home medications, including atenolol and terazosin, were restarted. He was discharged home with home health services for IV antibiotics and follow-up planned with oncology for radiation and chemotherapy resumption.

presenting with predominantly dry cough x2 weeks, fatigue x2

# Fever: Reported temp at home as high as 101, 100.8 at ED 
triage. No localizing symptoms except for cough which maybe 
chronic and congestion x2 weeks. Given history of GNR bacteremia 
due to cholangitis concern for there was concern for recurrent 
cholangitis. Additionally, bilirubin was elevated to 1.7 on 
admission which is higher than baseline. Antibioitics were held 
and the patent had a CT abdomen which raised concern for 
partially occluded stents. His case was discussed with the ERCP 
team, and given that he defevervesced, LFTs normalized and he 
was without abdominal pain, ERCP was not completed. The patient 
also had negative urine, blood cultures (x72 hours, final 
pending) and was ruled out for influenza. C. diff was not sent 
as he was having normal, formed stools.  His CT scan did not 
show any evidence of colitis.  Suspect that his symptoms may 
have been due to viral illness.  He does have mild leukopenia 
and mild thrombocytopenia, which could be due to viral illness, 
or alternatively to his chemotherapy.  
.
# Cholangiocarcinoma: s/p 5 cycles of Cis/Gem.  Patient will 
follow with his oncologist as an outpatient.

radiology_notes.text:
CHEST RADIOGRAPH PERFORMED ON ___

Comparison is made with a prior exam dated ___

CLINICAL HISTORY:  Fever, assess pneumonia.

FINDINGS:  PA and lateral views of the chest were provided.  Previously noted
PICC line has been removed.  A calcified granuloma is again noted in the right
mid lung.  There is mildly increased linear density at the left lung base
which is most compatible with atelectasis given the associated volume loss. 
Mild atelectasis is also noted at the right medial lung base.  Overall,
cardiomediastinal silhouette is normal.  No convincing signs of pneumonia.  No
effusion.  In the upper abdomen, metallic stents are present as well as
several surgical clips.  No free air is seen below the right hemidiaphragm.

IMPRESSION:  Basilar atelectasis without convincing signs of pneumonia. 
Interval removal of PICC line.

HISTORY:  ___ year old man with history of unresectable extrahepatic
cholangiocarcinoma and previous history of cholangitis presents with fever and
elevated bilirubin, concerns for recurrent obstruction.

COMPARISON:  CT abdomen pelvis from ___ and abdominal ultrasound
from ___ 

TECHNIQUE:  Volumetric CT acquisition of the abdomen and pelvis was performed
after administration of oral and 130 mL of Omnipaque 350 IV contrast material.
Post-processing reconstruction was performed in the coronal and sagittal
planes. 

DLP:  597 mGy-cm

FINDINGS:

There is atelectasis or scarring at the lung bases.  Normal heart size. 
Similar degree of intrahepatic biliary ductal dilatation of the right anterior
system along with pneumobilia of the left lobe.  2 common bile duct stents
remain in place.  There are two gold fiducial seeds present within the right
lobe of the liver.   The portal vein is patent.  The gallbladder is normal in
appearance.  Unchanged mildly prominent portacaval lymph nodes.  The adrenal
glands, kidneys, pancreas, and spleen are normal in enhancement. Stable left
renal cyst. The spleen remains enlarged, measuring approximately 16.8 cm. 
There are no enlarged retroperitoneal lymph nodes. Loops of small bowel are
normal in caliber without evidence of obstruction.  There is no free fluid or
free air.  The abdominal aorta is normal in caliber. Stable deformity of a
left posterior rib.

The colon is normal in appearance. The urinary bladder is unremarkable.  There
is no free fluid in the pelvis. No enlarged pelvic lymph nodes are noted. 
Multilevel degenerative disc disease.  

IMPRESSION:

1.  Stable intrahepatic biliary ductal dilatation with pneumobilia.  Two
common bile duct stents remain in place. Given the large degree of
pneumobilia, this suggests that the stent draing the left biliary system is
partially obstructed. 

2.  Resolved findings of colitis.
